evals.prompt: I have an original academic PDF and an existing translated Markdown paper whose figure locations are caption-only placeholders. Restore every substantive figure, including pages that mix vector diagrams and raster panels, while keeping the translation intact. Select complete crops by visually inspecting the source and deliver a portable Markdown bundle with a coverage report.
evals.expected_output: A non-destructive Markdown output with one complete, readable asset and marked insertion for each restored figure, plus a portable coverage report. The source Markdown remains unchanged.
expectations: The existing translated prose, captions, formulas, and other non-generated Markdown bytes are preserved without retranslation.
Every substantive PDF figure is explicitly accounted for as restore, already-present, skip with a reason, or blocked with a reason.
The model visually inspects each relevant PDF page and each generated crop; mixed vector and raster figure content is complete and unrelated body text is excluded.
Each restored figure has exactly one marker-delimited block and one portable relative image link, with no duplicate assets or blocks.
All generated links resolve inside a sibling asset directory and the output and report use portable relative names.
The workflow processes the supplied files locally and makes no external service or API call.

evals.prompt: Some figures in my translated Markdown are already linked, while other figure captions have no image. The document also contains a good structured Markdown table that must stay a table. Using the authoritative PDF, verify the existing assets, restore only missing substantive figures, and publish a non-destructive portable bundle and audit report.
evals.expected_output: A bundle that verifies and preserves existing images, inserts only missing figures, keeps the structured table byte-identical, and reports complete figure coverage with portable links.
expectations: The existing translated prose and the structured Markdown table are preserved byte-for-byte outside generated image blocks.
Already-present figures are verified and reported without copying, replacing, or duplicating their existing assets.
Missing substantive PDF figures are restored and every PDF figure is explicitly accounted for as restore, already-present, skip with a reason, or blocked with a reason.
The model visually inspects all selected pages and crops, and each restored crop contains the complete figure without adjacent captions or body text leaking in.
Each figure appears once at its matching caption with one marker block; all relative links resolve within the portable sibling bundle.
No unnecessary retranslation or prose rewrite occurs, and the helper does not call an external service.

evals.prompt: The PDF has two figures on the same page, but the translated captions have mismatched numbering and the visual-to-caption mapping is ambiguous. Reconcile the PDF and Markdown inventories without guessing, restore only mappings that are certain, and produce a report that makes any unresolved work explicit.
evals.expected_output: A safe non-destructive bundle in which unambiguous figures are restored once and ambiguous items are blocked with prominent reasons; the report says the result is incomplete when blocked work remains.
expectations: The model visually inspects the shared page and independently reconciles figure identity, numbering, captions, and boundaries before inserting anything.
An ambiguous or mismatched mapping becomes blocked with a prominent reason instead of being guessed or silently omitted.
When any figure is blocked, the coverage report says INCOMPLETE and the operation does not claim complete coverage.
Every unambiguous PDF figure is accounted for and appears at most once with no duplicate marker block or asset.
The original prose, captions, formulas, and structured tables remain unchanged outside generated blocks, with no unnecessary retranslation.
Any published image links are portable relative links inside the sibling asset directory, and no external call is made.
